question: m07
q: What rate are owner-occupiers actually paying on new variable loans, compared with the advertised rate?

transcript.answer:
**Owner-occupiers are paying about 6.2% on new variable loans, roughly 0.6 percentage points below the advertised discounted rate and about 2.6 points below the advertised standard rate.**

Latest comparable month, August 2026:

| Rate (owner-occupier, variable) | Aug 2026 |
|---|---|
| Advertised standard variable | 8.77% |
| Advertised discounted variable | 6.80% |
| **Actual, new loans funded (all institutions)** | **6.20%** |
| Actual, outstanding loans (all institutions) | 6.20% |

Sources: RBA tables F5 (advertised) and F6 (actual). The latest actual figure is August 2026; advertised rates run to September 2026, where the discounted rate is still 6.80%.

The gap has been fairly stable. In January 2025 the advertised discounted rate was 7.07% against an actual new-loan rate of 6.30% (a gap of about 0.77 points). It narrowed to about 0.55 points in late 2025. Both rates have moved up since early 2026: the new-loan rate went from 5.50% in January 2026 to 6.20% in August, and the advertised discounted rate from 6.05% to 6.80%.

The standard advertised rate is a poor guide to what people pay. Few borrowers pay it, so the discounted rate is the more realistic comparison.
